KHC.thesis_one_line: Maker of Heinz ketchup and Kraft cheese: cheap with a 6.8% dividend, but profits keep shrinking and debt ratings are under review.
kill_criteria: Adjusted EPS guidance midpoint for FY26 cut below $2.00 at any release.
North America organic volume/mix worse than -4.0 pp for two consecutive quarters.
Net Leverage (company definition: debt less cash and short-term investments over adjusted EBITDA, consolidated) above 3.5x, or Moody's downgrade below Baa3.
Dividend cut below $0.40 per quarter, or declared dividends exceeding free cash flow (consolidated operating cash flow less capex) over any four quarters.
FCF conversion below 90% of adjusted net income for a full year (would show working capital reversing).
key_adverse_facts: Q2'26 adjusted operating income -18.4%; FY26 guide constant-currency adjusted operating income -16% to -18% (top end lowered from -14%).
Goodwill/intangible impairments of 7.4bn in H1'26 and 9.3bn in FY25; Moody's Baa2 under review for downgrade, S&P and Fitch BBB negative outlook.
H1 FCF conversion of 123% is helped by supplier payment-term extension (terms up to 250 days).
Planned two-company split paused 11 Feb 2026; no structural catalyst.
data_conflicts: d4 trailing EPS -2.88 (GAAP, impairment-driven) vs adjusted EPS LTM 2.42; d4 FCF 3.25bn vs company H1 FCF 1.66bn annualised differences are timing.
Triage said 'revenue declining -1.4%' (Q2 figure, matches filing) and 'mid-way through split': filings say the split is PAUSED, not in progress.
KHC.next_earnings_date_basis: estimate from prior-year cadence (29 Oct 2025), not confirmed in a filing
KHC.confidence_in_thesis: low: cheap on cash flow but no evidence yet of volume stabilisation

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists. Price implies FCF -0.4% a year for ten years vs my base about 0%; the market already discounts a slight decline, so the stock is fair, not a bargain.

KHC.scenario_basis: Start adjusted EPS 2.06 (FY26E), price 23.63; base FY28 EPS 2.00 x 10.5 P/E plus $1.60/yr dividends; bear EPS 1.70 x 9.5 with dividend cut to $0.80 from year 2; bull EPS 2.45 x 12.5 with dividends maintained.

MAR.thesis_one_line: World's biggest hotel franchisor earning fees, not running hotels; a great business, but the share price already assumes years of strong growth.
kill_criteria: Worldwide comparable systemwide constant-dollar RevPAR growth below 1.0% for two consecutive quarters (company release, non-GAAP).
Net debt (consolidated total debt less cash) over trailing adjusted EBITDA above 3.5x.
Full-year adjusted EPS guidance midpoint cut below $11.40 at any release.
Net rooms growth below 4.0% year on year for two consecutive quarters.
Consolidated operating cash flow less capex (FCF) below 90% of GAAP net income for a full year.
key_adverse_facts: Price implies about 11-12% a year FCF growth for ten years (9.6% cost of equity; 8.5% at the originally used rate) vs my base about 7%; base 3-year return 4.6% a year.
Middle East RevPAR -43% in Q2'26, impact continuing into Q3.
Buybacks (1.8bn H1) plus dividends exceed FCF (1.5bn H1); debt 16.9bn, stockholders' deficit (4.5bn), net debt about 2.9x adjusted EBITDA.
Starwood data-breach litigation: about 100 suits, loss 'probable', accrual not material, further loss not estimable.
data_conflicts: d4 revenue 7.385bn is Q2-style total (income statement total revenues incl. reimbursements are about 26bn annual); fee revenue is the relevant measure.
d4 FCF 2.06bn vs my trailing FCF about 3.1bn (operating cash flow 3.73bn less capex 0.60bn): d4 appears to deduct contract acquisition costs twice.

MAR.confidence_in_thesis: high on business quality, low on return at this price

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists. Reverse DCF implies about 11-12% FCF growth a year at the program cost of equity of ~9.6% (8.5% at the originally used 8.5%) vs base about 7%; triage 'only 8.2% upside after +32%' agrees with WATCH. [DV27 2026-10-08: restated]

XYL.thesis_one_line: Water pumps, treatment and meters for utilities and industry: steadily widening profit margins at a fair price, but sales growth is slow and a new acquisition is pending.
kill_criteria: Organic revenue growth below 1.0% in two consecutive quarters (company release; Q2'26 was +1.3%).
Full-year adjusted EPS guidance midpoint cut below $5.45 at any release.
Consolidated net debt over adjusted EBITDA above 2.5x after the Cornell/Roper closing (short-term plus long-term debt less cash, 10-Q balance sheet).
Full-year free cash flow (operating cash flow less capex, consolidated) below 9.0% of revenue, or H2 FCF below 0.65bn.
Backlog (ex the single large contract) shrinking year on year for two consecutive quarters, or cancellation of that contract.
key_adverse_facts: Organic revenue +0.5% in H1'26; FY organic guide cut to 2-3% from 2-4%.
Q2 orders +42% driven by one significant Water Solutions and Services contract (segment organic orders +147%); Water Infrastructure orders -3.9% organic.
CFO resigned 13 Aug 2026 (8-K Item 5.02), 16 days after raising guidance.
$1.46bn cash acquisition of Cornell Pump and Roper Pump (closing Q4 2026) financed with $1.5bn notes at 5.25-5.85%; target earnings not disclosed in filings opened.
GAAP EPS is 24% below adjusted EPS (intangible amortization, restructuring, loss on sales).
data_conflicts: d4 forward EPS 6.25 is FY27-type consensus; FY26 company guide is 5.55-5.70 adjusted.
d4 total debt 3.055bn includes leases vs consolidated balance sheet debt 2.926bn.
XYL.next_earnings_date_basis: estimate from prior-year cadence (28 Oct 2025), not confirmed in a filing
XYL.confidence_in_thesis: medium: margin expansion is evidenced in filings; volume growth and deal integration are not yet proven

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists. Reverse DCF implies 6.5% FCF growth a year vs my base about 7.5%; modest margin of safety, hence half weight.
